wstep: This card describes bratwurst, a mild fresh German-style sausage, following the UGA Extension recipe. [T:MIE-141]

akapity: Fresh sausage is raw: keep it in the refrigerator and cook it thoroughly before eating. [T:MIE-138]
UGA recommends cooking products made from ground pork and beef to an internal temperature of 160 °F. [T:MIE-021]
Meat: 10 pounds pork trim (70% lean). [T:MIE-141]

Seasoning: salt 6 1/2 tablespoons (3.2 oz), ground white pepper 1 1/2 tablespoons (0.3 oz), sugar 1 3/4 teaspoons (0.3 oz), mace 1/2 tablespoon (0.1 oz) and onion powder 1 tablespoon (0.2 oz). [T:MIE-141]
Liquid: 1 cup water, or 3 pounds ice. [T:MIE-141]
Casings: natural hog casings or 32 mm collagen casings. [T:MIE-141]
Fresh sausage is made from ground meat mixed with seasonings, and it must be refrigerated and thoroughly cooked before eating. [T:MIE-138]
Keep the meat and other ingredients refrigerated at 40 °F or below (about 4 °C), also while you work, and check with a thermometer. [T:MIE-138]
If you will not cook the sausage right away, put it back in the refrigerator as soon as it is made. [T:MIE-138]
Grind the pork through a 1/4-inch plate and mix it with the salt, water and spices. [T:MIE-141]
Stuff the mixture into the casings. [T:MIE-141]
Cook the sausages in steam or water at 170 °F (about 77 °C). [T:MIE-141]
The UGA recipe stops at an internal temperature of 155 °F (about 68 °C), but the same bulletin recommends 160 °F for products made from ground pork. [T:MIE-141,MIE-021]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): cook the bratwurst until a thermometer shows 160 °F (about 71 °C) inside. [T:MIE-142]
According to the FDA, color and texture are unreliable signs of safety, and a food thermometer is the only way to be sure. [T:MIE-117]
Store bratwurst in the refrigerator. [T:MIE-141]

JarAtlas rule (cautious): treat cooked bratwurst without nitrite as cooked meat, which the FDA chart gives 3–4 days in the refrigerator, not the 2–4 weeks given for smoked sausages with salt and nitrite. [T:MIE-142,MIE-137]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): throw away cooked bratwurst that has been in the refrigerator for more than 4 days. [T:MIE-142,MIE-137]
According to UGA Extension, fresh sausage keeps 7–10 days in the refrigerator at 35–40 °F, or 4–6 months in the freezer. [T:MIE-028]
NCHFP gives a shorter limit for raw red meat: keep it at 40 °F (about 4 °C) or below and use it within 3–5 days, or freeze it. [T:MIE-110]
The FDA storage chart gives raw sausage from pork, beef, chicken or turkey 1–2 days in the refrigerator at 40 °F (4 °C). [T:MIE-137]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): use raw fresh sausage within 2 days, the shortest of these limits, or freeze it. [T:MIE-137,MIE-110,MIE-028]
JarAtlas rule (cautious): throw away raw fresh sausage that has been in the refrigerator for more than 2 days. [T:MIE-137,MIE-028]
Do not keep sausage out of the refrigerator for more than 2 hours, or for more than 1 hour when the temperature is above 90 °F (about 32 °C). [T:SLO-408]
